messages.author: c09cdb35cca40b8e
messages.subject: geom_boxplot() and large datasets
parts:
Dear ggplot2 mailing list,

I love ggplot2 and am moving a load of reporting code into ggplot2 for standardisation of visualisation. I work within the field of pharmaceutical development, and within gene expression profiling typically have 30,000 rows x 40 columns that I would like to summarise in a boxplot. The standard R boxplot works just fine but with ggplot2 things are a little slow (and I haven't yet been patient enough for visualisation to complete)

My question is simple, how would anyone recommend plotting a boxplot with large data dimensions.

At the moment I have implemented a simple hack where assuming that the matrix is within a data.frame "df" I

require(random)
data <- melt(df[as.numeric(randomNumbers(n=1000, min=1, max=nrow(df))),])

The structure of the data is good enough, but in cases I am losing some outlier resolution. Is this hack sufficient or have I overlooked some trivial techniques that I should have applied first?

Cheers

Stephen
